question: What are the candidate therapeutic targets, immune pathways and biomarkers in ulcerative colitis with the strongest convergent evidence?

models.orchestrator: Claude Opus 5.5 — Claude Code main session
models.agents: Claude Sonnet 5.5 — Claude Code subagents (agente-expresion, agente-literatura, agente-externo, agente-celular, agente-vias, agente-aplicado)

datasets.url: https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/opentargets/platform/26.09/output/credible_set/ (200 parts, filtered to GTEx-v10 colon gene eQTL, CEDAR colon/rectum eQTL and OTAR2057 IBDverse sc-eQTL studies, p < 5e-8)
https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/opentargets/platform/26.09/output/credible_set/ (200 parts, filtered to studyType pqtl and studyId UKB_PPP_EUR*)

findings.statement: CXCR2 tops the convergence ranking: pooled UC vs control log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814], up in all eight cohorts, with a paired inflamed vs non-inflamed rise [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972] and a small rise in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399]. It is a neutrophil receptor, so the bulk signal largely reflects neutrophil infiltration (to be checked by the cell-context specialist); genetic association and CXCR1 and CXCR2 antagonists in clinical trials add support.

CXCL8 (interleukin-8), the ligand of CXCR1 and CXCR2, is up in all eight cohorts with pooled log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864], and the change holds after adjusting for colon segment, age and sex in MSCCR [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=2.499]. It marks local neutrophil-driven inflammation; part of the signal is infiltrate-derived.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in all eight cohorts, pooled log2FC [gene=CD274; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.974]. It is largely local to inflamed mucosa: almost no change in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=CD274; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.1971]. This is an inflammation-induced checkpoint response with immune-cell contribution; it supports a checkpoint-agonist rather than an antagonist direction.

HMGCS2, an epithelial ketogenesis gene, is lost in all eight cohorts, pooled log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.838]. The loss is local to inflamed mucosa: paired inflamed vs non-inflamed [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.9508] but no change in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649]. A local-inflammation biomarker of epithelial metabolic failure, not a target.

CHI3L1 is among the strongest and most reproducible increases, pooled log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.875] in all eight cohorts, and it holds after covariate adjustment in MSCCR. At protein level the change is in the same direction (log2 ratio [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607]) but the proteomics authors did not call it significant and the protein change is far smaller than the RNA change.

MMP3 is up in all eight cohorts, pooled log2FC [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.901], and replicates at protein level in independent inflamed mucosa, significant by the authors' call [gene=MMP3; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.806]. Stromal and tissue-remodelling MMPs form a coherent replicated module, though broad MMP inhibitors have a poor clinical record.

IDO1 (tryptophan catabolism) is up in all eight cohorts, pooled log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.118], and local to inflamed mucosa in the paired contrast. It looks like an interferon-driven feedback response with immune and epithelial sources; inhibitors exist but would be pursued only if the signal is shown to be pathogenic.

JAK2 has a modest pooled increase [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.8744], significant in all eight cohorts. Its convergence rank rests on genetics and drug tractability rather than on a large expression change, so expression alone does not distinguish it; the action of JAK inhibitors is on signalling, not transcript level.

DUOX2 (epithelial hydrogen peroxide generation, with its partner DUOXA2) is up in all eight cohorts, pooled log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.4116], and is among the strongest inflamed-mucosa markers in the paired contrast. It reflects an epithelial antimicrobial response and is a biomarker candidate, not a clear target.

AQP8 shows the strongest loss in the pooled analysis [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.246], significant in most cohorts. It is an epithelial water-transport gene, consistent with loss of mature absorptive colonocytes; a biomarker of epithelial dysfunction, rarely a target.

CLDN8 is strongly lost in all eight cohorts, pooled log2FC [gene=CLDN8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.291]. As a tight-junction gene its loss fits barrier dysfunction; a biomarker rather than a target.

IL1B is up in all eight cohorts, pooled log2FC [gene=IL1B; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.87]. As a myeloid cytokine, much of the bulk increase probably comes from infiltrating neutrophils and monocytes rather than a change inside the tissue; interleukin-6 and CCL2 show the same pattern, and drug approvals exist for interleukin-1 and interleukin-6 blockade in other diseases.

REG1A has a large pooled increase [gene=REG1A; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.486] but is significantly up in only six of eight cohorts with high heterogeneity, so it is less reproducible than CXCL8, CHI3L1 or MMP3; REG3A behaves similarly.

caveats: Microarray fold changes are compressed; only directions and significance are compared across cohorts.
Heterogeneity (I2) is high for nearly all top genes, so pooled sizes are approximate.
Immune and neutrophil genes (CXCR2, CXCL8, IL1B, S100A8/9, TREM1) may reflect infiltrating cells; composition adjustment is left to the cell-context specialist.
Protein replication was checked for only two genes (CHI3L1, MMP3) and the proteomics cohort is small; not measured is not evidence against a gene.
Covariate-adjusted analysis was run only for CXCL8 and CHI3L1.
Non-inflamed vs control changes were read for CXCR2, CD274 and HMGCS2 only.

findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top-ranked gene (meta-analysis upregulation [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814]) with clinical-stage antagonists (reparixin, navarixin, ladarixin, SX-682) in Open Targets, but the verbatim-validated literature-relation set for CXCR2 is empty. Literature support in this corpus comes only from abstract chunks, e.g. a title 'CXCR1 and CXCR2 are potential neutrophil extracellular trap-related treatment targets in ulcerative colitis: insights from Mendelian randomization, colocalization and transcriptomic analysis', and a CXCL5/CXCR2 eQTL/pQTL/transcriptome study linking the axis to neutrophil chemotaxis in UC. These are bioinformatic/genetic signals; no UC trial evidence for CXCR2 antagonists appears in the corpus.

The literature states that the CXCL8 axis with its receptors CXCR1 and CXCR2 participates in UC pathogenesis through PI3K/Akt, MAPK and NF-kappaB signaling; CXCL8 is also a hub gene in a PPI analysis and a blood diagnostic candidate for IBD in RNA-seq validation. Expression is strongly up in the meta-analysis [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864]. Evidence is review/bioinformatic level; anti-IL-8 antibody ABX-IL8 only reaches an early clinical stage in Open Targets.

A single mouse and human study reports IDO1 elevated in UC patients and correlated with pro-inflammatory macrophage polarization; IDO1 induced that polarization via the ER stress GRP78-XBP1 pathway, and the inhibitor methyl-tryptophan ameliorated DSS colitis (weight loss, colon shortening, severity). Preclinical, single study; IDO1 inhibitors (epacadostat, linrodostat) have oncology history only.

CHI3L1 is upregulated in UC patients and correlates with NLRP3 inflammasome expression; the same study reports it promotes macrophage pyroptosis via BCAT1/NF-kappaB, and exogenous NF-kappaB activation reversed the protective effect of CHI3L1 inhibition. Another study confirmed binding of velpatasvir to recombinant CHI3L1 by microscale thermophoresis. No approved or clinical-stage drug for CHI3L1 in UC; evidence is preclinical and from a few studies.

MMP1 shows strong diagnostic potential for UC-associated CRC in one bioinformatic study, where ilomastat was only predicted in silico as an inhibitor. Separately, MMP1 is among transcripts modified by mirikizumab that correlate with Mayo, Geboes and Robarts indices, i.e. a treatment-responsive activity marker rather than a validated target. Broad MMP inhibitors (marimastat, doxycycline) have no UC evidence in this corpus.

DUOX2 protein is among the most elevated proteins in inflamed UC biopsies versus healthy controls, and an eight-gene bioinformatic panel including DUOX2 is proposed for UC diagnosis and therapy. A herbal formula (TLXDS) is reported to alleviate UC by inhibiting DUOX2 overexpression, reducing inflammation and ferroptosis, with DUOX2 'may serve as a key therapeutic target'. Mostly bioinformatic and herbal-pharmacology evidence; no DUOX2 drug exists.

One study reports AQP9 predominantly expressed in neutrophils (single-cell and immunofluorescence), upregulated in UC mouse colon, and promoting NET formation via JAK2-STAT3-mediated pyroptosis to aggravate epithelial injury. This indicates the AQP9 signal is neutrophil-derived (infiltrating immune cells) rather than epithelial. Mouse colitis models confirm overexpression. Single-study, no drug.

S100A9 expression is reported to perform excellently in diagnosing active UC by ROC analysis and is overexpressed in UC by nanopore RNA-seq. In the tofacitinib study, S100A9 was downregulated in resident macrophages with response. Atractylenolide-I is reported to restore barrier function via S100A9/AMPK/mTOR. Evidence is biomarker-grade and preclinical; no S100A9-directed drug.

CXCL1 is proposed as a UC diagnostic/activity marker in several bioinformatic studies, but its individual discrimination is modest: in one of them it ranked below CYP2R1, NEU4 and LPCAT1 as an activity marker. It is also among nine genes overexpressed in both pancolitis regions.

SLC26A2 is down-regulated in active UC mucosa versus healthy controls, with decreased levels correlating with Mayo score and PUCAI, and it correlates negatively with IL-17A and positively with CLDN3 in colon tissue. Single study; downregulated epithelial genes of this type may reflect loss of epithelial identity rather than a drug target.

HMGCS2 is reported decreased in UC with high diagnostic value in two bioinformatic studies, consistent with the strong downregulation seen across cohorts. Evidence is diagnostic-signature level only; no mechanistic or therapeutic study in the corpus.

LCN2 is upregulated in UC and shared with CRC in IBD. In one study, LCN2 was highest in short-duration UC, lower in long-duration UC and lower again in UC-associated cancer, though all exceeded normal, so it is proposed for carcinogenesis related to disease duration rather than as a monotonic marker.

caveats: CXCR1, CXCR2, CD274, FCGR2A, JAK2, IL2RA, INHBA, TREM1, CXCL5, PI3, S100A12, REG1A and CDH3 have little or no verbatim-validated literature relations despite strong expression/Open Targets support; the literature stream for them is Open Targets literature score only. CD274 literature is chunk-level only (PD-L1 validated by immunohistochemistry in one series; named a UC hub gene). Tofacitinib is approved for UC, and one study reports differential macrophage effects contribute to non-response, but JAK2 has no gene-linked literature relation.
Most literature relations are from bioinformatic hub-gene or diagnostic-signature studies and single preclinical mouse studies; they are not clinical validation.
Several studies concern UC-associated CRC or IBD in general, not UC alone.
Numeric AUC values in sentences were not bound to numeric fields and so are described in words.
Corpus is about 585 abstracts, so absence of a relation is not absence of literature in PubMed.

findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top convergence gene: up in biopsies in all cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814]), with Open Targets genetic association, small-molecule and antibody tractability, and clinical antagonists (reparixin phase three; navarixin, ladarixin, danirixin, elubrixin, SX-682 phase two). It has no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, so MR is not tested (absence of evidence only).

CXCR2 has many papers in mouse colitis (including the antagonist SB225002 ameliorating acute colitis), but MGI has no curated single-gene colitis phenotype. Not strongly constrained and no known safety events or pleiotropic traits sharing the genetic signal; its Reactome pathways are neutrophil degranulation, chemokine receptor binding and G alpha(i) signalling.

CD274 (PD-L1) is the best example of blood MR and biopsy expression agreeing in direction of benefit: genetically higher plasma protein lowers UC risk, colocalises with the IBD GWAS and replicates in FinnGen and Liu 2023 [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]. Because it is up in UC mucosa while protein is protective, this argues for a protective, compensatory induction, so inhibiting it (existing anti-PD-L1 drugs) would be the wrong direction; agonism is the therapeutic logic.

CD274 MR sensitivity: Steiger direction is correct and Egger intercept is not significant, but heterogeneity is present [gene=CD274; type=mr_sensitivity; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; layer=plasma_protein; heterogeneity_p=0.0259]. LOEUF is moderate and not flagged as strongly constrained [gene=CD274; type=target_safety; source=DATASET:SAFETY; loeuf=0.476]; no known safety events listed, although checkpoint blockade is not a UC-safe direction. No gut eQTL instrument (not tested).

IL12B is an established UC target and the strongest plasma MR hit: higher protein raises UC risk, so inhibition is protective, colocalising with the IBD GWAS and replicating in FinnGen and Liu 2023 [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]. It validates the MR design as a positive control. Safety: not strongly constrained; shared genetic signal with psoriasis, mouth ulcers and vasculitis traits, and MR heterogeneity is highly significant.

IL10 is a genetically protective cytokine: one cis-pQTL Wald ratio shows higher plasma protein lowers UC risk, colocalising with the GWAS and replicating in FinnGen [gene=IL10; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.071]. The single instrument makes the effect size implausibly large; the direction supports an anti-inflammatory axis rather than an inhibitor target.

CXCL8 is among the most strongly and consistently induced genes in all cohorts, with a phase two anti-interleukin-8 antibody and literature support, but has zero Open Targets genetic association and plasma MR is null with no replication [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289]. It is better as an activity biomarker and ligand of the CXCR1 and CXCR2 axis than as a genetically supported target.

CXCL5 is up in UC biopsies in all cohorts, yet genetically higher plasma protein lowers UC risk and replicates in FinnGen and Liu 2023, without colocalisation and using a tag variant [gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634]. Blood genetics oppose the biopsy direction, a caution against blocking ELR+ chemokines on expression alone; it is expression-led with no drug.

IDO1 is strongly induced in biopsies and has clinical-stage inhibitors (linrodostat phase three) and many mouse colitis papers, but has no Open Targets genetic association and plasma MR is not significant [gene=IDO1; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.111]; colon eQTL MR is also not significant. Expression-led, genetically unsupported.

SLC26A3 expression is lower (decreased) in UC biopsies in all cohorts [gene=SLC26A3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-1.702]. In gut cell-type eQTL MR (OLFM4+ crypt progenitor enterocytes), the genetic estimate is risk-raising for UC, colocalising and replicating in FinnGen [gene=SLC26A3; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.607]. Single instrument, one cell type; the tissue loss is likely a consequence of epithelial damage rather than the causal direction. Tissue and genetics disagree; no cis-pQTL (plasma not tested).

JAK2 is the top-ranked known UC target by Open Targets association, but shows only a small expression change in biopsies, so genetic support is not matched by strong tissue change; the other known UC targets in the list (JAK3, TYK2, IL23A, TNF, ITGA4, ITGB7, S1PR1) are drug targets already.

Strongest colon-tissue eQTL MR signals include IRF5 and IRF8, where higher expression in transverse colon raises UC risk with GWAS colocalisation, implicating innate and interferon regulatory transcription factors; these are single-instrument results in a different layer from plasma protein.

caveats: Plasma protein is not mucosal protein; most top expression genes (CXCR2, CXCL8, MMPs, S100A8/9, CHI3L1) lack a cis-pQTL or gut eQTL, so not tested is not evidence against them.
Single-instrument MR estimates (IL10, SLC26A3) have inflated effect sizes and cannot be tested for pleiotropy.
Convergence scores weight tractability and literature; many top genes have zero Open Targets genetic association.
Drugs listed come from Open Targets records in any indication, not UC-specific trials.
Findings on S1PR1, TNF etc. were not individually queried; only convergence_ranking and disease_top_targets were used for them.

findings.statement: CXCR2 is made almost entirely by neutrophils in inflamed UC mucosa in Gubatan (neutrophil share of transcripts [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]). Smillie assigns T/NK, but only one of the other three atlases (the anti-TNF atlas) agrees, since Garrido-Trigo and Gubatan give myeloid, so the attribution is not replicated; the Smillie call reflects neutrophils being absent from that dataset. The bulk increase is partly composition, with a retained fraction after cell-proportion adjustment of [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.17]. CXCR2 is a marker of neutrophil influx; any drug effect would act on neutrophils, not on resident tissue.

CXCR1 behaves like its partner receptor CXCR2, a neutrophil receptor: the neutrophil share of its transcripts in inflamed mucosa is [gene=CXCR1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.962]. The fraction of the bulk change that survives adjustment for cell composition is [gene=CXCR1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.195] (partly_composition); the adjustment may over-correct for activation, but the signal is chiefly neutrophil arrival.

CXCL8 is myeloid in Smillie (macrophages, inflammatory monocytes, DC2) and replicates in Garrido-Trigo, Gubatan and the anti-TNF atlas (all three agree), but in Gubatan neutrophils make a neutrophil share of [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873] of its transcripts. After composition adjustment the change loses significance (adjusted padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0523], verdict composition). It is a marker of myeloid/neutrophil influx rather than a tissue-intrinsic target; loss of significance is not proof of pure influx.

AQP9 is myeloid in Smillie and in all three other atlases (Garrido-Trigo, Gubatan, the anti-TNF atlas), so replicated, but the neutrophil share of its transcripts in Gubatan is [gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92]. The retained fraction after composition adjustment is [gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.261], so AQP9 is mainly a neutrophil-influx marker with a modest residual tissue change.

MMP1 is made by stromal cells, chiefly inflammatory fibroblasts (Smillie stromal lineage share [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.871]); stromal is dominant in Garrido-Trigo, Gubatan and the anti-TNF atlas, so the attribution replicates in all three. Neutrophils make only a small share of transcripts. The bulk change persists after adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636], partly_composition), and Visium deconvolution names inflammatory fibroblasts as the in-situ source. This is a tissue-intrinsic fibroblast signal.

DUOX2 is epithelial (Smillie epithelial lineage share [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947]), replicated in Garrido-Trigo, Gubatan and the anti-TNF atlas, with enterocytes the top state; Xenium and Visium deconvolution also place it in epithelium. It keeps a significant change after composition adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161]), which is strong evidence of an epithelium-intrinsic change; neutrophils contribute little.

CHI3L1 is stromal in Smillie (lineage share [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.941], inflammatory fibroblasts) and replicates in Garrido-Trigo and the anti-TNF atlas, but Gubatan gives myeloid (neutrophils contribute substantially there), so two of three other atlases agree. The change survives adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967]), supporting an intrinsic fibroblast change with some neutrophil contribution.

IDO1 is myeloid in Smillie (macrophages, DC1) and in Garrido-Trigo and the anti-TNF atlas, but epithelial in Gubatan (enterocytes), so the lineage call is replicated by two of three atlases with a mixed epithelial/myeloid source. The neutrophil share is minor ([gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.072]). The change persists after adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505]), consistent with interferon-driven induction inside the tissue.

CD274 (the PD-L1 gene) has a diffuse source: Smillie gives myeloid with a low lineage share (plasma, macrophages), replicated in Garrido-Trigo and Gubatan while the anti-TNF atlas gives T/NK; in Gubatan the neutrophil share of transcripts is [gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]. The change is retained after adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978]), so it is both an influx and a tissue effect.

HMGCS2 is down in UC and is epithelial (Smillie lineage share [gene=HMGCS2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.982]), replicated in Garrido-Trigo, Gubatan and the anti-TNF atlas. The decrease persists after adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=-0.8548]), indicating an intrinsic loss of the epithelial metabolic (ketogenic) programme, partly also loss of mature epithelial cells.

caveats: Composition adjustment uses estimated proportions and can over-correct when resident cells become activated; a loss of significance is not proof of pure influx.
Smillie has no neutrophils, so neutrophil-derived genes (CXCR2, CXCR1, AQP9, CXCL8) can be mis-assigned there; Gubatan is the reference for neutrophil share.
Shares compare cell types, not tissue abundance. Spatial data were queried only for DUOX2 and MMP1. Genes not examined beyond the ranking: CXCL1, MMP10, S100A8, IL1B, TREM1, LCN2, MMP3.

findings.statement: PROGENy JAK-STAT activity is increased in all eight cohorts with none decreasing, with very strong t values in the largest cohort. This is a robust, already drug-targeted axis (JAK inhibitors), but one of many pathways raised together.
The STAT3 regulon is up in all eight cohorts, consistent with IL-6/gp130/OSM-family signalling. Inferred from target genes, not STAT3 mRNA.

TNFa and NFkB PROGENy pathways are up in all eight cohorts with no cohort decreasing, and the RELA regulon is also up in all eight. TNF is already drug-targeted, so this confirms a validated axis rather than a new one.
EGFR, TGFb and Hypoxia pathways are each up in all eight cohorts, none down. Broad stress and repair programs: replicated but non-specific, and none is an established UC drug axis here.
Negative result: the p53 pathway is not increased in any cohort and is lower in three; it is not a consistent inflamed-UC signal. Androgen is also heterogeneous (up in two, down in three cohorts).

CXCL8 is the top-ranked cytokine candidate (third in convergence): log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864], up in all eight cohorts. Smillie bulk-lineage attribution is myeloid macrophages (replicated in three other atlases), but in Gubatan single cell the transcripts are mostly neutrophil, mainly Neutrophil CXCR4, Neutrophil and Neutrophil OSM states. Only Phase 2 anti-IL-8 drugs exist (ABX-IL8, adakitug).

CXCR2 ranks first in convergence (up in all eight cohorts, genetics and tractability both high; CXCR2 antagonists navarixin, reparixin, ladarixin, SX-682 are in phase two and phase three trials, mostly outside UC). Its transcripts are neutrophil-dominated in Gubatan, whereas Smillie assigns T/NK and that lineage call is not replicated across atlases, so the source is infiltrating neutrophils rather than a tissue-resident change.

Neutrophil-to-neutrophil CXCL8-CXCR2 circuit: Neutrophil CXCR4 sends to Neutrophil receivers and the score rises strongly in inflamed versus uninflamed mucosa (largest log2 change among the top pairs), an autocrine/paracrine recruitment loop. Co-expression, not proof of signalling.

Neutrophil CXCL8 also reaches ACKR1 endothelial cells (atypical chemokine receptor that presents chemokine for transmigration); Neutrophil CXCR4 to ACKR1 endothelial is the highest-scoring CXCL8 pair in inflamed mucosa. ACKR1 is not a currently drugged target.

Negative or weak result for the neutrophil OSM to fibroblast circuit: OSM-IL6ST scores toward LP fibroblasts are about two orders of magnitude below the CXCL8 pairs, and Neutrophil OSM to LP and crypt-bottom fibroblasts fall in inflamed versus uninflamed mucosa. Neutrophil OSM-to-fibroblast signalling is not supported as a dominant circuit by this co-expression data.

IL1B is up in all eight cohorts. Monocyte-derived macrophages signal through IL1R2 to neutrophil states with high co-expression scores. IL1R2 is a decoy receptor, so this may dampen rather than drive signalling. IL-1 blockade (canakinumab) is approved for other diseases, not UC.

TREM1 is up in all eight cohorts with the Phase 2 drug nangibotide, but no ligand-receptor pair passes expression thresholds in the single-cell dataset, so its sender-receiver circuit cannot be resolved here.
IDO1 is up in all eight cohorts and has literature support but no genetic evidence; drugs (epacadostat, linrodostat) exist from oncology only. A repurposing candidate, not UC-validated.

caveats: Pathway and TF activities are inferred from target genes in bulk biopsies and reflect cell composition (neutrophil/monocyte infiltration) as much as tissue-intrinsic change.
Inflamed mucosa activates many pathways at once; most PROGENy pathways are up in nearly all cohorts, so they are weak discriminators.
Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression, not evidence of signalling; only top pairs per gene were returned.
IL-23 and integrin genes were not queried individually.

findings.statement: PROGENy TNFa activity is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]) but also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]), so it marks severity rather than a ustekinumab mechanism; PURSUIT placebo shows nothing (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]).

JAK-STAT activity is associated with non-response to ustekinumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) with UNIFI placebo borderline (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0543]); it is not significant for golimumab or vedolizumab after correction.

CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking (six evidence streams, same direction in all eight cohorts, phase two to three antagonists such as reparixin and navarixin) with a meta-analysis log2FC of [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814].

Higher baseline CXCR2 is associated with ustekinumab non-response (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]) but also with UNIFI placebo non-response (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]) and the drug-vs-placebo interaction is null (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.982]): a neutrophil-severity marker, not a drug-specific mechanism. Golimumab, infliximab and vedolizumab do not survive correction.

CXCL8 is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102]) and in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0154]), so it marks severity; the faecal calprotectin correlation in PROTECT is not significant.

In the adalimumab single-cell atlas (GSE282122, a small cohort of remitters and non-remitters) CXCL8 shows no baseline difference between remitters and non-remitters in any cell state; after treatment it falls in cycling mononuclear phagocytes and rises in enterocyte and transit-amplifying states. Lead only.

OSM is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]) while UNIFI placebo does not reach significance (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]); however the drug-vs-placebo interaction is not significant (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.982]), so drug specificity is not established. No anti-TNF arm survives correction.

TREM1 is associated with ustekinumab non-response (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) but also separates UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]), consistent with a general severity signal.

IDO1 does not separate ustekinumab non-responders after correction (padj [gene=IDO1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.14]) yet does separate UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=IDO1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0289]); no drug-specific signal.

CHRDL2 is the top first-in-class candidate (meta log2FC [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=2.36]), antibody-tractable, no clinical drug; its signal is stromal (inflammatory fibroblasts) and replicated across Smillie 2019, Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122. Composition is only partly retained, so part of the increase reflects fibroblast expansion; no response or genetic evidence supplied.

CPXM1 is a stromal candidate (inflammatory fibroblasts and WNT2B+ fibroblasts) replicated in Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122 but not Gubatan 2026, where epithelial is dominant; composition only partly retained and no functional evidence in the record.

LAX1 is assigned to T/NK in Smillie 2019 and GSE282122 but to plasma cells in Garrido-Trigo 2023 and Gubatan 2026, so the lineage attribution is not replicated; it is an immune-infiltration signal with partly composition-driven increase, not a tissue-intrinsic target.

XKR9 is the only top-list candidate classified as intrinsic (retained share [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.7976]), epithelial, with low vital-organ RNA, but it is up in only a minority of cohorts, so replication is weak.

caveats: Response analyses are baseline associations, not predictions; UNIFI has few responders so power differs by arm.
Most non-responder signals in ustekinumab also appear in UNIFI placebo, indicating severity; golimumab, infliximab, vedolizumab, etrolizumab and ACT1 arms have small n and rarely survive correction.
Discovery candidates lack genetic, functional and response evidence; stromal and T/NK candidates are partly composition-driven.
The adalimumab single-cell cohort is small.

summary.text: The strongest convergent signal in ulcerative colitis mucosa is the neutrophil chemokine axis. CXCR2 leads the convergence ranking: it is up in all eight cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814]), has Open Targets genetic support and clinical-stage antagonists in other indications. But neutrophils make almost all of its transcripts (share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]), and only a small fraction of the change survives composition adjustment ([gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.17]). Its Smillie lineage call (T/NK) is confirmed by only one of the three other single-cell atlases, because neutrophils are missing from that atlas. The axis is best read as neutrophil recruitment: a druggable but unapproved target and a strong marker of influx.

Several leading genes are changes inside the tissue rather than arriving cells, and their cell source now replicates across four single-cell atlases (Smillie 2019, Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and the anti-TNF atlas of Thomas 2024). MMP1 is made by inflammatory fibroblasts and keeps its change after adjustment ([gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]); DUOX2 is epithelial and keeps its change too ([gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161]); both are placed in the same compartment in tissue sections.

Human genetics separates targets from markers. Genetically higher plasma IL12B raises UC risk ([gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]), the positive control of the design, while higher plasma CD274 lowers it ([gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]), so PD-L1 induction in inflamed mucosa looks protective and blocking it would be the wrong direction. CXCL8 has no causal support (plasma MR [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289]).

The epithelial programme of absorption and ketogenesis is lost locally: HMGCS2 falls in all eight cohorts ([gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.838]) only in inflamed mucosa, and AQP8 shows the largest loss ([gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.246]). These are markers of epithelial failure rather than drug targets.

Treatment response mostly tracks severity. CXCR2 is higher in ustekinumab non-responders ([gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]) but also in placebo non-responders ([gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]), and the drug-by-placebo interaction is null ([gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.982]). The first-in-class screen proposes CHRDL2, a stromal gene whose fibroblast source replicates in all four atlases, as the leading new hypothesis for laboratory testing.

expression.text: CXCL8 is up in all eight cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864]) and holds after adjustment for colon segment, age and sex ([gene=CXCL8; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=2.499]).

The largest reproducible increases are stromal and epithelial: CHI3L1 ([gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.875]), MMP3 ([gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.901]) and DUOX2 ([gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.4116]), each up in all eight cohorts. REG1A rises as much ([gene=REG1A; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.486]) but is significant in only six of eight cohorts with high heterogeneity, so it is less reproducible.

The strongest losses are epithelial: AQP8 ([gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.246]), CLDN8 ([gene=CLDN8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.291]) and HMGCS2 ([gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.838]), consistent with loss of mature absorptive colonocytes, the barrier and ketogenesis.

inflammation.text: HMGCS2 is lost only where the mucosa is inflamed: paired inflamed vs non-inflamed [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.9508] against no change in non-inflamed mucosa ([gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649]).

CXCR2 rises locally in the paired contrast ([gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972]) but also a little in non-inflamed mucosa ([gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399]); CD274 changes almost only in inflamed mucosa.

replication.text: The leading increases replicate in every cohort and, where mass spectrometry measured them, as protein: MMP3 rises in independent inflamed mucosa ([gene=MMP3; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.806]), while the CHI3L1 protein change is in the same direction but small and not significant ([gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607]).

literature.text: The published literature supports the CXCL8 axis with its receptors CXCR1 and CXCR2 in UC pathogenesis through NF-kappaB and MAPK signalling, mostly at review and bioinformatic level; for CXCR2 itself there are only genetic and transcriptomic papers and no UC trial of its antagonists.

Functional evidence exists for a few candidates. One mouse and human study links IDO1 to pro-inflammatory macrophage polarization, and its inhibition eased DSS colitis. CHI3L1 promotes macrophage pyroptosis through NF-kappaB. AQP9, mainly a neutrophil gene, drives neutrophil extracellular traps. MMP1, DUOX2, HMGCS2 and S100A9 rest on diagnostic or expression studies.

external.text: Approved and established UC targets sit high in Open Targets (JAK2 leads by association), and IL12B is the strongest plasma MR hit ([gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]), colocalising and replicating in FinnGen. CXCR2 has genetic association and phase two and three antagonists but no instrument, so MR is not tested.

Genetics and tissue disagree for several induced genes. Higher plasma CD274 is protective ([gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]), and so is higher CXCL5 ([gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634]) and IL10 ([gene=IL10; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.071], single instrument), a caution against blocking genes on their rise alone. CXCL8 and IDO1 have no causal support ([gene=IDO1; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.111]).

In gut eQTL MR the disagreement also runs the other way: SLC26A3 is lower in UC biopsies ([gene=SLC26A3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-1.702]), yet the estimate in crypt progenitor enterocytes is risk-raising ([gene=SLC26A3; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.607]), colocalising and replicating in FinnGen. With one instrument in one cell type, the tissue loss is more likely a consequence of epithelial damage than the causal direction. IRF5 and IRF8 lead the colon-tissue eQTL results.

cells.text: Cell attribution was checked in four single-cell atlases folded into five shared lineages: Smillie 2019, Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 (the only one with neutrophils) and the anti-TNF atlas of Thomas 2024, typed into lineages in this project. A lineage counts as replicated when at least two of the three other atlases agree. Neutrophils make most of the transcripts of CXCR2 ([gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]), CXCR1 ([gene=CXCR1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.962]) and AQP9 ([gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92]); for CXCR2 only the anti-TNF atlas agrees with Smillie, while Garrido-Trigo and Gubatan give myeloid.

After composition adjustment little of these changes remains: CXCR2 keeps [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.17], CXCR1 [gene=CXCR1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.195] and AQP9 [gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.261] of the change, and CXCL8 loses significance ([gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0523]) although its myeloid source replicates in all three other atlases. The adjustment can over-correct when resident cells become activated, so a lost change is not proof of pure influx.

Tissue-intrinsic changes: MMP1 (stromal, [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.871] of transcripts in Smillie, replicated in all three other atlases; adjusted [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]), DUOX2 (epithelial, [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947], replicated in all three; adjusted [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161]) and CHI3L1 (stromal, [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.941], two of three; adjusted [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967]). HMGCS2 is epithelial in all four atlases and its loss survives adjustment ([gene=HMGCS2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=-0.8548]); IDO1 has a mixed myeloid and epithelial source (two of three) and keeps its change ([gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505]).

spatial.text: In tissue, Visium deconvolution names inflammatory fibroblasts as the source of MMP1 and the epithelium as the source of DUOX2, which Xenium single cells confirm; tissue and the four single-cell atlases agree for both.

pathways.text: JAK-STAT, TNFa and NFkB activity and the RELA and STAT3 regulons are up in all eight cohorts with none decreasing; JAK and TNF are already drugged, so these confirm validated axes.
EGFR, TGFb and hypoxia programmes are also up in every cohort but are broad stress and repair signals. p53 is not raised in any cohort: a negative result.

The most specific circuit is neutrophil to neutrophil: CXCL8 to CXCR2 rises the most in inflamed mucosa, and neutrophil CXCL8 also reaches ACKR1 endothelium, the transmigration route. The neutrophil OSM to fibroblast circuit is weak and falls in inflamed mucosa. Monocyte IL1B pairs with the IL1R2 decoy, which may dampen signalling. Co-expression is not proof of signalling.

treatment.text: TNFa pathway activity is higher before treatment in ustekinumab non-responders ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]) and in UNIFI placebo non-responders ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]), so it marks severity; JAK-STAT is similar ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]).

CXCR2, CXCL8 and TREM1 separate ustekinumab non-responders and also placebo non-responders (TREM1 placebo [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]). OSM is significant for ustekinumab only ([gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]; placebo [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]) but its interaction is null ([gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.982]). In the adalimumab single-cell atlas CXCL8 shows no baseline difference between remitters and non-remitters.

discovery.text: CHRDL2 leads the first-in-class candidates (meta log2FC [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=2.36]): an antibody-tractable stromal gene of inflammatory fibroblasts with no clinical drug, whose lineage is the same in all four atlases. Part of its rise reflects fibroblast expansion, and no genetic or response evidence exists yet.

CPXM1 is a stromal candidate whose source replicates in Garrido-Trigo 2023 and the anti-TNF atlas but not in Gubatan 2026, where epithelium dominates; its rise is only partly kept after composition adjustment.

LAX1 does not replicate (T/NK in two atlases, plasma cells in two) and is an immune-infiltration signal. XKR9 is the only intrinsic candidate (retained share [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.7976]), but it rises in a minority of cohorts.

integration.text: Expression, single cells, genetics and tractability agree that the neutrophil chemokine axis dominates the inflamed mucosa, and disagree on what it means: CXCR2 is druggable and genetically associated, but its signal is cell arrival, not tissue change, and its link to poor response is shared with placebo.

The candidates where tissue change, replicated cell source across four atlases and in-situ location agree are MMP1, DUOX2 and CHI3L1; genetics is silent for them. Where genetics speaks, it sometimes opposes the expression direction (CD274, CXCL5), which argues for agonism or caution rather than blockade.

limitations.text: Public data only; nothing here was tested in the laboratory or in patients.
Only Gubatan 2026 captures neutrophils, so neutrophil genes cannot agree in the other three atlases; the lineage replication rule is weakest for them.
The anti-TNF atlas (Thomas 2024) was typed into lineages from canonical markers in this project, not with the authors' cell states; it has no neutrophil cluster.
The composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells become activated.
Most expression-led candidates have no genetic instrument, so 'not tested' is not evidence against them.
Treatment-response arms other than UNIFI are small, and no gene separates a drug from placebo after correction; the adalimumab single-cell cohort has six remitters.
Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression, not proof that a signal is used.

targets.rationale: Ranks first on convergence: up in all eight cohorts, with genetic association and clinical-stage antagonists. Kept first as a neutrophil-recruitment target, not a tissue target: neutrophils make most of its transcripts ([gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]), only one of three other atlases confirms its Smillie lineage, little survives adjustment, and its link to ustekinumab non-response is shared with placebo.

Positive control: the strongest plasma MR result, higher protein raises UC risk ([gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]), matching the approved drugs of the ustekinumab class.

A fibroblast change that holds: stromal in all four atlases, placed in inflammatory fibroblasts in tissue and kept after adjustment ([gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]). Broad MMP inhibitors failed elsewhere, so selectivity is the open question.

Strong and reproducible ([gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864]), myeloid and neutrophil-made, loses significance after adjustment and has no genetic support: a marker of influx and severity more than a target.

Epithelial in all four atlases and in tissue, with a change kept after adjustment ([gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161]); an epithelial antimicrobial response with no drug.

Among the largest increases ([gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.875]), stromal in three of four atlases and kept after adjustment; functional studies link it to macrophage pyroptosis, but the protein change is small.

Known UC target class (JAK inhibitors): leads Open Targets association but shows only a modest expression change ([gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.8744]); its rank rests on genetics and drugs.

Up in all eight cohorts ([gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.118]) with a tissue-kept change and functional colitis data, but no genetic support and only oncology inhibitors: a repurposing lead.

Higher plasma PD-L1 is protective ([gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]): its induction in inflamed mucosa looks compensatory, so the therapeutic logic is agonism, not blockade.

Up in all eight cohorts and replicated as protein ([gene=MMP3; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.806]); a tissue-remodelling marker.
Lost only in inflamed mucosa ([gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.838]), epithelial in all four atlases: a marker of local epithelial metabolic failure.

Exploratory: the leading first-in-class candidate, antibody-tractable, stromal in all four atlases (meta log2FC [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=2.36]); partly fibroblast expansion, no genetics yet.
Exploratory: stromal first-in-class candidate replicated in two of three other atlases; partly composition-driven and without functional evidence.
